chunks: Abu Abdillah عليه السلام was asked about a man who rented land from the kharaj land for a specified amount of dirhams or a specified quantity of food.

He then leases it out by the jarib or by separate plots for a known amount, so that he gains a surplus over what he rented from the authorities, while spending nothing. Or he leases that land in plots on condition that he gives them the seeds and the expenses, so that he gains a surplus over his rental payment, and the upkeep of the land is upon him. Is that permitted for him, or is it not?
He عليه السلام said: If you rent land and spend something on it, or repair it, then there is no harm in what you mentioned.

key_terms.بِدَرَاهِمَ مُسَمًّى: for a specified amount of dirhams
key_terms.جَرِيبًا جَرِيبًا: parcel by parcel, measured by jarib
key_terms.فَضْلٌ: surplus or profit above the original rental
key_terms.ٱلسُّلْطَانِ: the ruling authority from whom the land was rented

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh to sublease kharaj land for a profit?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about subleasing kharaj land for profit. The permissibility is tied to the renter's expenditure or maintenance of the land, indicating that profit is allowed when accompanied by real input, cost, or repair.
